The CDB is described as a OneTroy document developed collaboratively by administrators and department heads from both high schools together with the teaching and learning team, and it is updated each year as part of the district's curriculum review process. The most consequential change is a restructured science and English pathway: newly developed Chemistry 1 and 9 English courses become required for all students beginning with the class of 2027, while Active Chemistry/Earth Science and the two existing English 9 courses are removed.
2023_079_cdb_updates_23_24.page:
Purpose
The High-School Course Description Book (CDB) sets out course requirements and opportunities for Troy School District high school students. It is organized by department so that students and families understand the offerings. It is identified as a OneTroy document developed collaboratively by administrators and department heads from both high schools and the teaching and learning team. The CDB is updated annually as part of the curriculum review process, with department teams determining where course descriptions should be updated to reflect new curriculum and instruction, and where courses should be added or deleted. The report lists the changes made for the 2023/2024 school year.

Courses Added

| Course | Grades | Length / Credit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chemistry 1 | 9-12 | 1 semester, ½ credit, No Retake | Newly developed revision of the previously taught full year Chemistry class; required for all students beginning with the class of 2027; satisfies ½ credit of the math related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year |
| Chemistry 2 | 9-12 | 1 semesters, ½ credit, No Retake | Pre-requisite: Chemistry 1; in development, to begin running in the second semester of the 23/23 school year; satisfies 1/2 credit of the math related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year; pre-requisite for Advanced Placement Chemistry |
| 9 English | 9th grade | 2 semesters, 1 credit, ½ credit per semester | Newly developed revision of previously taught 9th grade English courses; required for all students beginning with the class of 2027 |
| Intensified Algebra 1 | Grades 9 | 2 semesters, 1 credit per semester, No retake | Prerequisite: None; currently being piloted at THS and AHS; scheduled in collaboration with the math specialist |
| Mindful Art | — | 1 semester, ½ credit per semester, Retakes: 1 | New course designed in collaboration with the counseling and art departments |

Course Content Highlights
Chemistry 1 covers energy, atomic structure, bonding, chemical reactions, solution, and combustion, with analytical problem solving of real-life phenomena and laboratory techniques. Chemistry 2 extends this to atomic structure, bonding, chemical reactions, solutions, acid-base chemistry, thermodynamics, equilibrium, and gas laws, noting that a strong foundation in algebra is important and that students interested in any STEM related field are encouraged to take it. 9 English is a foundational course emphasizing in-depth study of multiple genres of reading and modes of writing and speaking, with novels, short stories, poetry, nonfiction texts, mentor texts, and book clubs, and essays including literary analysis, informational, argumentative, and narrative. Intensified Algebra 1 targets conceptual understanding, mathematical skills, and problem-solving and reasoning, including metacognition and multiple representations of linear, absolute value, quadratic, rational, polynomial, power, and exponential functions; successful completers will be prepared for Geometry. Mindful Art combines mindfulness concepts with art activities addressing personal identity, stress reduction and coping skills, relationship skills through collaboration and community work, and gratitude.

Courses Removed
Advanced Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness (to be combined with lifeguarding as Lifeguarding, Advanced Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness); Active Chemistry/Earth Science (both removed due to the newly restructured science course pathway); Beginning & Intermediate Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness (combined with Learning to Swim as Learning to Swim: Beginning & Intermediate Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness); Emerging Engineering (re-titled Mechatronics); English 9 Literature and Compositions and English 9 Literature and Composition Honors (removed in favor of the newly designed required English course beginning with the class of 2027); Intermediate Tumbling and Gymnastics (combined with Beginner Tumbling and Gymnastics); Metals 1 and Advanced Metals (removed due to lack of student interest over the past several years, rising material costs, and safety concerns).

Course Descriptions Updated
Advanced Placement Biology: description updated and GBBE removed as a pre-requisite. Algebra 2 Honors, Geometry Honors, and Precalculus Honors: prerequisites updated to show ability to move tracks. Team Sports courses will no longer have gender attached.
2023_079_cdb_updates_23_24.verbose:
Presented to the Troy School District Board of Education for the February 7, 2023 meeting, this administrative report describes updates to the High-School Course Description Book (CDB) for the 2023/2024 school year.

Background and process
The High-School Course Description Book shows the course requirements and opportunities for students and is organized by department so that students and families have an understanding of the offerings. It is characterized as a OneTroy document developed collaboratively by administrators and department heads from both high schools together with the teaching and learning team. The CDB is updated annually as part of the district's curriculum review process; each year department teams work to determine where course descriptions should be updated to reflect new curriculum and instruction, or where courses should be added or deleted.

COURSES ADDED

Chemistry 1. Described as the newly developed course, a revision of the previously taught full year Chemistry class, required for all students beginning with the class of 2027. Catalog line: Grades 9-12. 1 semester. ½ credit. No Retake. The course satisfies ½ credit of the math related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year. Students will study theories and concepts in chemistry related to energy, atomic structure, bonding, chemical reactions, solution, and combustion. Many topics are developed through analytical problem solving of real-life phenomena. Experiments will be performed which will drive the learning of concepts, and students will execute a variety of laboratory techniques throughout the semester. Students are expected to work with a group, follow procedures, ask questions, organize data, make observations, develop models, and apply concepts learned to real-life.

Chemistry 2. The report states the course is in development and will begin running in the second semester of the 23/23 school year. Students interested in taking a full year of chemistry in order to access AP Chemistry will enroll in both Chemistry 1 and Chemistry 2. Catalog line: Grades 9-12. 1 semesters. ½ credit. No Retake. Pre-Requisite: Chemistry 1. The course satisfies 1/2 credit of the math related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year. Students will extend their learning of theories and concepts of chemistry related to atomic structure, bonding, chemical reactions, solutions, acid-base chemistry, thermodynamics, equilibrium, and gas laws. Many topics are developed through analytical problem solving of real-life phenomena, and experiments will be performed in a collaborative setting which will drive the learning of concepts. A strong foundation in algebra will be important in understanding class concepts. Students interested in any STEM related field are encouraged to take the course, and the course is a pre-requisite for taking Advanced Placement Chemistry.

9 English. Identified as the newly developed 9th grade English course, a revision of previously taught 9th grade English courses, required for all students beginning with the class of 2027. Catalog line: 2 semesters. 1 credit. ½ credit per semester. This foundational English course is required for all 9th grade students. Completion of both 9th and 10th grade English courses will prepare students to engage with future English courses including Advanced Placement should they elect to do so. The course offers a rigorous curriculum and includes in-depth study and analysis of multiple genres of reading and a variety of modes of writing and speaking in a class structure that allows students the opportunity to practice skills and strategies daily. This repertoire of skills and strategies enables students to approach reading, writing, and speaking experiences with confidence and proficiency. Students hone their reading skills through frequent and increased engagement with novels, short stories, poetry, nonfiction texts, mentor texts, and book clubs. Daily writing in the forms of drafts and revisions based on teacher modeling and timely feedback will lead to skilled final essays which include literary analysis, informational, argumentative, and narrative. Class structure, including dedicated in-class time for reading, writing, and speaking, choice, and frequent timely feedback, will foster growth in students' reading, writing, and speaking skills.

Intensified Algebra 1. The report states the course is currently being piloted at THS and AHS. It covers all content of Algebra I as well as additional enrichment skills to build background knowledge quickly to ensure success in future high school math courses. Catalog line: Grades 9. 2 semesters. 1 credit per semester. No retake. Prerequisite: None. The course is scheduled in collaboration with the math specialist. It targets conceptual understanding, mathematical skills, and problem-solving and reasoning. Students are re-engaged in the curriculum through visualizations and multiple representations of mathematical ideas. Students also study metacognition to motivate and build students' positive beliefs about their academic abilities. Content includes multiple representations of linear, absolute value, quadratic, rational, polynomial, power, and exponential functions. The course builds foundational math skills used throughout high school, and students who successfully complete it will be prepared for Geometry.

Mindful Art. A new course designed in collaboration with the district's counseling and art departments. Catalog line: 1 semester. ½ credit per semester. Retakes: 1. Mindful Art combines mindfulness concepts with engaging art activities to encourage expression, self-awareness, and stress reduction. The class will focus on exploring personal identity, learning about and practicing stress reduction and coping skills, developing relationship skills through collaboration and community work, and fostering gratitude.

COURSES REMOVED

Advanced Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness is to be combined with lifeguarding; the new course name will be Lifeguarding, Advanced Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness.

Active Chemistry and Earth Science: both courses are being removed due to the newly restructured course pathway for science.

Beginning & Intermediate Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness will be combined with Learning to Swim; the new course name will be Learning to Swim: Beginning & Intermediate Swimming and Lifetime Sports & Fitness.

Emerging Engineering is re-titled Mechatronics.

English 9 Literature and Compositions and English 9 Literature and Composition Honors: both courses are being removed to show the newly designed required English course beginning with the class of 2027.

Intermediate Tumbling and Gymnastics will be combined with Beginner Tumbling and Gymnastics.

Metals 1 and Advanced Metals are being removed due to lack of interest by students over the past several years. The report adds that the course was becoming costly due to rising prices of materials, and that safety was also a concern in the course.

COURSE DESCRIPTIONS UPDATED

Advanced Placement Biology: course description updated and GBBE removed as a pre-requisite.

Algebra 2 Honors, Geometry Honors, and Precalculus Honors: prerequisites updated to show ability to move tracks.

Team Sports courses will no longer have gender attached.

Significance
The additions and removals together restructure two required freshman pathways. In science, the full-year Chemistry class is replaced by a semester-length Chemistry 1 required of the class of 2027 onward, with an optional companion Chemistry 2 leading to Advanced Placement Chemistry, while Active Chemistry and Earth Science exit the catalog. In English, the two former ninth-grade offerings, English 9 Literature and Compositions and English 9 Literature and Composition Honors, are replaced by a single required 9 English course, also beginning with the class of 2027. Remaining changes consolidate overlapping physical education and swimming offerings, retire the metals program on cost, interest, and safety grounds, retitle Emerging Engineering as Mechatronics, and remove gender designations from Team Sports courses.
